message.content: How does the router stamp time on packets when device clocks drift?
How does the router stamp time on packets when device clocks drift?

injected.body: Device clocks drift a few seconds a day, so the router stamps packets on arrival.
injected.label: Clock drift

injected.body: The router drops any packet whose CRC-16 checksum does not match its payload.
injected.label: Checksum

injected.body: The router's queue holds at most ten thousand packets before it sheds the oldest.
injected.label: Queue limit

injected.body: Gateways upload packets in batches every five minutes to save radio power.
injected.label: Batch upload

injected.body: A device resends a packet after eight seconds when no acknowledgement arrives.
injected.label: Retry window

injected.body: A device that sends nothing for an hour is marked dead in the route table.
injected.label: Dead device

injected.body: Each sensor packet starts with a two-byte header naming the device and its firmware.
injected.label: Packet header

injected.body: The route table maps each device ID to the gateway nearest its grove row.
injected.label: Route table

injected.body: A packet payload is limited to fifty-one bytes on the slow radio setting.
injected.label: Payload size

injected.body: Firmware 3.2 added a temperature field to the packet payload.
injected.label: Firmware 3.2

injected.body: Raising the gateway antenna two meters fixed the dropped packets from row twelve.
injected.label: Antenna fix

injected.body: Soil sensors in the grove report moisture and temperature in each packet.
injected.label: Grove sensors

injected.body: A sensor in cold room B sends a packet when the temperature rises above two degrees.
injected.label: Storage sensor

injected.body: The label printer in the packing shed prints the batch number on each crate.
injected.label: Label printer

injected.body: Drip irrigation runs at night when the soil sensors report dry ground.
injected.label: Water schedule

near_misses.body: A weekly report sums crates picked and packets received per grove row.
near_misses.label: Weekly report

near_misses.body: The spray log records each orchard treatment with its date and row.
near_misses.label: Spray log

near_misses.body: A frost alarm wakes the orchard manager when the grove sensor reads below zero.
near_misses.label: Frost alarm

part.content:
The router handles clock drift between devices by stamping packets with its own arrival time rather than relying on the device's internal clock. Since device clocks can drift a few seconds a day, the router uses its own stable clock to timestamp packets as they arrive. This means the router records the time when it actually receives the packet, ensuring consistent timing regardless of any drift in the sending device's clock. This arrival-based timestamp helps the router maintain accurate timing and sequencing information in its routing table and communication processes.
